description.p: Aerie brings Google Drive to the Linux desktop with a native, fast and quiet experience.
Browse and search My Drive, move files in and out, and keep chosen folders in sync. Aerie talks to Google directly from your computer; no other service sees your files or sign-in.
Click the pause badge in the sidebar to resume syncing.
Resume a paused sync from the sidebar, or with Sync Now.
Fixes a sync loop caused by macOS .DS_Store files on Drive.
A sync activity view: every change in the current sync, grouped by where it stands.
Filter the sidebar to show only synced shared drives.
Synced drives show a badge in the sidebar.
Shows "Starting Aerie" while the background service starts, instead of asking to connect.
A progress bar and the current file while syncing.
Synced folders keep their place in Drive's folder structure on this computer.
A toolbar button keeps the open folder in sync.
Sync all of My Drive or an entire shared drive.
Right-click a folder to keep it in sync.
A design pass: the luminous Aerie mark, a refreshed welcome screen, a richer file list, foldable and pinnable shared drives, and a sync and storage panel.
Drag the sidebar's edge to resize it.
Dropping files from a file manager uploads them.
Shared drives appear as soon as Aerie opens, with a loading indicator during the first index.
The file list keeps your selection and scroll position while Aerie indexes.
An unfinished index continues where it stopped after a restart or upgrade.
Uploads and file actions work while Aerie indexes, uploads show where they're going, and sign-in renews after sleep.
Paces requests to stay within Google Drive's rate limits, and retries quietly when Google asks Aerie to slow down.
Choose which shared drives to index; others load on demand.
The Aerie look, shared drives, a separate sync service and sync badges on folders.
First development build.
